title_en: Enterprise State-owned Assets Law of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en: Article 1 This Law is formulated for the purposes of maintaining the basic economic system of the country, consolidating and developing the state-owned economy, strengthening the protection of state-owned assets, giving play to the leading role of the state-owned economy in the national economy, and promoting the development of the socialist market economy.

Article 2 For the purposes of this Law, "state-owned assets of enterprises" (hereinafter referred to as "state-owned assets") means the rights and interests formed by the state's capital contributions to enterprises in various forms.
Article 3 State-owned assets belong to the state, i.e., to the whole people. The State Council shall, on behalf of the state, exercise the ownership of state-owned assets.

Article 4 The State Council and the local people's governments shall, in accordance with the provisions of laws and administrative regulations, on behalf of the state, perform the functions of a contributor to the state-invested enterprises and enjoy the rights and interests of a contributor.
For large state-invested enterprises determined by the State Council to be related to the lifeline of the national economy and national security, and state-invested enterprises in fields such as important infrastructure and important natural resources, the State Council shall perform the functions of a contributor on behalf of the state. Other state-invested enterprises shall be subject to the performance of the functions of a contributor by the local people's governments on behalf of the state.

Article 5 For the purposes of this Law, "state-invested enterprises" means wholly state-owned enterprises, wholly state-owned companies, and state-controlled companies and state-participating companies with state capital contributions.

Article 6 The State Council and the local people's governments shall, in accordance with the law, perform the functions of a contributor in line with the principles of separating government functions from enterprise management, separating social public management functions from the functions of a state-owned assets contributor, and not interfering with the independent operation of enterprises in accordance with the law.

Article 7 The state shall take measures to promote the concentration of state-owned capital in important industries and key areas that are related to the lifeline of the national economy and national security, optimize the layout and structure of the state-owned economy, promote the reform and development of state-owned enterprises, improve the overall quality of the state-owned economy, and enhance the controlling and influential power of the state-owned economy.

Article 8 The state shall establish and improve a state-owned assets management and supervision system that is compatible with the development requirements of the socialist market economy, establish and improve an assessment system for the preservation and appreciation of state-owned assets and a system for accountability, and fulfill the responsibility for the preservation and appreciation of state-owned assets.
Article 9 The state shall establish and improve a basic management system for state-owned assets. Specific measures shall be formulated in accordance with the provisions of the State Council.
Article 10 State-owned assets shall be protected by law, and no entity or individual may infringe upon them.

Article 11 The state-owned assets supervision and administration institution of the State Council and the state-owned assets supervision and administration institutions established by the local people's governments in accordance with the provisions of the State Council shall, based on the authorization of the people's government at the same level, perform the functions of a contributor on behalf of the people's government at the same level for state-invested enterprises.
The State Council and the local people's governments may, as needed, authorize other departments or institutions to perform the functions of a contributor on behalf of the people's government at the same level for state-invested enterprises.
The institutions and departments that perform the functions of a contributor on behalf of the people's government at the same level are hereinafter collectively referred to as "institutions performing the functions of a contributor."

Article 12 An institution performing the functions of a contributor shall, on behalf of the people's government at the same level, enjoy the rights of a contributor with respect to state-invested enterprises, including the right to receive asset returns, participate in major decision-making, and select managers, in accordance with the law.
An institution performing the functions of a contributor shall, in accordance with the provisions of laws and administrative regulations, formulate or participate in formulating the articles of association of state-invested enterprises.
Where an institution performing the functions of a contributor deals with a major matter relating to the performance of the functions of a contributor that, as stipulated by laws, administrative regulations, and the people's government at the same level, requires approval by the people's government at the same level, it shall submit the matter to the people's government at the same level for approval.

Article 13 A shareholder representative assigned by an institution performing the functions of a contributor to attend a shareholders' meeting or a general meeting of shareholders convened by a state-controlled company or a state-participating company shall, in accordance with the instructions of the assigning institution, propose motions, express opinions, exercise voting rights, and promptly report to the assigning institution on the circumstances and results of the performance of his duties.

Article 14 An institution performing the functions of a contributor shall perform the functions of a contributor in accordance with laws, administrative regulations, and the articles of association of the enterprise, protect the rights and interests of the contributor, and prevent losses of state-owned assets.
An institution performing the functions of a contributor shall safeguard the rights that the enterprise enjoys according to law as a market entity, and shall not interfere in the business activities of the enterprise except when performing the functions of a contributor in accordance with the law.

Article 15 An institution performing the functions of a contributor shall be responsible to the people's government at the same level, report to the people's government at the same level on the performance of the functions of a contributor, accept supervision and assessment by the people's government at the same level, and be responsible for the preservation and appreciation of state-owned assets.
An institution performing the functions of a contributor shall, in accordance with the relevant provisions of the state, periodically report to the people's government at the same level on the aggregated analysis of the total amount, structure, changes, and returns of state-owned assets.

Article 16 A state-invested enterprise shall, in accordance with laws, administrative regulations, and the articles of association of the enterprise, enjoy the rights to possess, use, benefit from, and dispose of its movable property, immovable property, and other property.
The right to autonomous operation and other legitimate rights and interests enjoyed by a state-invested enterprise in accordance with the law shall be protected by law.

Article 17 A state-invested enterprise engaged in business activities shall comply with laws and administrative regulations, strengthen business management, improve economic efficiency, accept the management and supervision implemented by the people's government and its relevant departments and institutions according to law, accept supervision by the public, assume social responsibility, and be responsible to the contributor.
A state-invested enterprise shall, in accordance with the law, establish and improve its corporate governance structure, and establish and improve internal supervision, management, and risk control systems.

Article 18 A state-invested enterprise shall, in accordance with laws, administrative regulations, and the provisions of the finance department of the State Council, establish and improve financial and accounting systems, set up accounting books, conduct accounting, and provide true and complete financial and accounting information to the contributor in accordance with laws, administrative regulations, and the articles of association of the enterprise.
A state-invested enterprise shall distribute profits to the contributor in accordance with laws, administrative regulations, and the articles of association of the enterprise.

Article 19 Wholly state-owned companies, state-controlled companies, and state-participating companies shall establish a board of supervisors in accordance with the provisions of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China. For wholly state-owned enterprises, the institution performing the functions of a contributor shall, in accordance with the provisions of the State Council, assign supervisors to form a board of supervisors.
The board of supervisors of a state-invested enterprise shall, in accordance with laws, administrative regulations, and the articles of association of the enterprise, supervise the conduct of directors and senior officers in performing their duties, and conduct supervision and inspection over the financial affairs of the enterprise.
Article 20 A state-invested enterprise shall, in accordance with the provisions of laws, implement democratic management through the workers' congress or other forms.

Article 21 A state-invested enterprise shall, according to law, enjoy the rights of an investor over the enterprise in which it has invested, such as the right to receive asset returns, to participate in major decision-making, and to select managers.

A state-invested enterprise shall, in accordance with the provisions of laws and administrative regulations, establish an internal supervision, management and risk control system with clear rights and responsibilities and effective checks and balances, by formulating or participating in the formulation of the articles of association of the enterprise in which it has invested, so as to safeguard its rights and interests as an investor.

Article 22 The institution performing the functions of a contributor shall, in accordance with the provisions of laws, administrative regulations and the articles of association of the enterprise, appoint or remove, or recommend the appointment or removal of, the following persons of a state-invested enterprise:
(1) appointing or removing the manager, deputy manager, person in charge of financial affairs and other senior officers of a wholly state-owned enterprise;
(2) appointing or removing the chairman, vice-chairman, directors, chairman of the board of supervisors and supervisors of a wholly state-owned company; and
(3) proposing candidates for directors and supervisors to the shareholders' meeting or the general meeting of shareholders of a state-controlled company or a state-invested company without controlling interest.
Directors and supervisors who shall be held by representatives of the employees in a state-invested enterprise shall be democratically elected by the employees in accordance with the provisions of relevant laws and administrative regulations.

Article 24 The institution performing the functions of a contributor shall, in accordance with the prescribed conditions and procedures, examine the candidates for directors, supervisors and senior officers to be appointed or recommended for appointment. Those who pass the examination shall be appointed or recommended for appointment in accordance with the prescribed authority and procedures.

Article 25 Without the consent of the institution performing the functions of a contributor, the directors and senior officers of a wholly state-owned enterprise or a wholly state-owned company shall not hold a concurrent post in any other enterprise. Without the consent of the shareholders' meeting or the general meeting of shareholders, the directors and senior officers of a state-controlled company or a state-invested company without controlling interest shall not hold a concurrent post in any other enterprise engaged in the same type of business.
Without the consent of the institution performing the functions of a contributor, the chairman of the board of directors of a wholly state-owned company shall not concurrently serve as manager. Without the consent of the shareholders' meeting or the general meeting of shareholders, the chairman of the board of directors of a state-controlled company shall not concurrently serve as manager.
Directors and senior officers shall not concurrently serve as supervisors.

Article 26 The directors, supervisors and senior officers of a state-invested enterprise shall abide by laws, administrative regulations and the articles of association of the enterprise, shall owe a duty of loyalty and a duty of diligence to the enterprise, and shall not take advantage of their positions to accept bribes or obtain other illegal income and improper benefits, shall not misappropriate or embezzle the assets of the enterprise, shall not decide on major matters of the enterprise beyond their authority or in violation of procedures, and shall not commit any other acts that infringe upon the rights and interests of the contributors of state-owned assets.

Article 27 The State shall establish a system for assessing the business performance of the managers of state-invested enterprises. The institution performing the functions of a contributor shall conduct annual and term assessments of the managers it appoints, and shall decide on rewards and penalties for the managers based on the assessment results.
The institution performing the functions of a contributor shall, in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State, determine the remuneration standards for the managers of state-invested enterprises it appoints.

Article 28 The principal persons in charge of wholly state-owned enterprises, wholly state-owned companies and state-controlled companies shall undergo the term economic responsibility auditing conducted according to law.

Article 29 Where the State Council or a local people's government provides that the managers specified in subparagraphs (1) and (2) of paragraph 1 of Article 22 of this Law shall be appointed or removed by the people's government at the corresponding level, such provisions shall prevail. The institution performing the functions of a contributor shall, in accordance with the provisions of this Chapter, assess, reward and penalize the aforesaid managers and determine their remuneration standards.

In major matters such as merger, division, restructuring, listing, increase or decrease of registered capital, issuance of bonds, making major investments, providing large amount guarantees for others, transfer of major assets, making large amount donations, distribution of profits, and dissolution and application for bankruptcy, a state-invested enterprise shall comply with the provisions of laws, administrative regulations, and the enterprise's articles of association, and shall not harm the rights and interests of investors and creditors.

The merger, division, increase or decrease of registered capital, issuance of bonds, distribution of profits, and dissolution and application for bankruptcy of a wholly state-owned enterprise or wholly state-owned company shall be decided by the institution performing the duties of a contributor.

For a wholly state-owned enterprise or wholly state-owned company regarding a matter listed in Article 30 of this Law, except for matters decided by the institution performing the duties of a contributor in accordance with Article 31 of this Law and relevant laws, administrative regulations, and the enterprise's articles of association, the matter shall be decided by collective discussion of the enterprise's responsible persons for a wholly state-owned enterprise, and by the board of directors for a wholly state-owned company.

For a state-controlled company or state-parameter company regarding a matter listed in Article 30 of this Law, the matter shall be decided by the company's shareholders' meeting, general meeting of shareholders, or board of directors in accordance with laws, administrative regulations, and the company's articles of association. If decided by the shareholders' meeting or general meeting of shareholders, the shareholder representative appointed by the institution performing the duties of a contributor shall exercise the rights in accordance with Article 13 of this Law.

For merger, division, dissolution, application for bankruptcy of an important wholly state-owned enterprise, wholly state-owned company, or state-controlled company, and for major matters that, according to laws, administrative regulations, and the provisions of the people's government at the same level, shall be reported by the institution performing the duties of a contributor to the people's government at the same level for approval, the institution performing the duties of a contributor shall, before making a decision or giving instructions to the shareholder representative appointed by it to attend the shareholders' meeting or general meeting of shareholders of the state-controlled company, report to the people's government at the same level for approval.
The important wholly state-owned enterprises, wholly state-owned companies, and state-controlled companies referred to in this Law shall be determined in accordance with the provisions of the State Council.

If relevant laws and administrative regulations provide that matters such as issuance of bonds and investment by a state-invested enterprise shall be submitted to the people's government or the relevant departments or institutions of the people's government for approval, verification, or filing, the matter shall be handled in accordance with those provisions.

A state-invested enterprise shall, when making investments, comply with the national industrial policies and conduct feasibility studies in accordance with national regulations; when transacting with others, it shall be fair and for value, and obtain reasonable consideration.

For major matters such as merger, division, restructuring, dissolution, and application for bankruptcy of a state-invested enterprise, opinions of the enterprise's trade union shall be solicited, and opinions and suggestions of employees shall be solicited through the employees' representative congress or other forms.

A wholly state-owned enterprise, wholly state-owned company, or state-controlled company shall, when performing the duties of a contributor regarding major matters of enterprises in which it invests, refer to the provisions of this Chapter. The specific measures shall be formulated by the State Council.

Enterprise restructuring shall be decided by the institution performing the duties of a contributor or by the company's shareholders' meeting or general meeting of shareholders in accordance with statutory procedures.
For restructuring of an important wholly state-owned enterprise, wholly state-owned company, or state-controlled company, the institution performing the duties of a contributor shall, before making a decision or giving instructions to the shareholder representative appointed by it to attend the shareholders' meeting or general meeting of shareholders of the state-controlled company, submit the restructuring plan to the people's government at the same level for approval.

Enterprise restructuring shall be conducted by formulating a restructuring plan, which shall specify matters such as the organizational form of the enterprise after restructuring, the plan for handling enterprise assets and creditor's rights and debts, the plan for equity changes, the operational procedures for restructuring, and the selection and engagement of intermediaries such as asset appraisal and financial audit.
If enterprise restructuring involves re-placement of enterprise employees, an employee placement plan shall also be formulated and shall be reviewed and approved by the employees' representative congress or the employees' congress.

Enterprise restructuring shall, in accordance with regulations, carry out asset verification, financial audit, and asset appraisal, accurately define and verify assets, and determine the value of assets objectively and fairly.
If enterprise restructuring involves converting non-monetary assets such as physical assets, intellectual property, and land use rights of the enterprise into state capital contributions or shares, the assets to be converted shall be appraised in accordance with regulations, and the appraised confirmed price shall be the basis for determining the amount of state capital contributions or the number of shares. Property shall not be converted into shares at a low price, nor shall any other act harming the rights and interests of contributors be carried out.

An affiliate of a state-invested enterprise shall not seek improper benefits by taking advantage of transactions with the state-invested enterprise, harming the interests of the state-invested enterprise.
Affiliates as referred to in this Law mean the directors, supervisors, senior officers of the enterprise and their close relatives, as well as enterprises owned or actually controlled by such persons.

A wholly state-owned enterprise, wholly state-owned company, or state-controlled company shall not provide funds, commodities, services, or other assets to affiliates without compensation, nor shall it conduct transactions with affiliates at unfair prices.

Transactions between a state-controlled company or state-parameter company and its affiliates shall be decided by the company's shareholders' meeting, general meeting of shareholders, or board of directors in accordance with the Company Law of the People's Republic of China, relevant administrative regulations, and the company's articles of association. If decided by the shareholders' meeting or general meeting of shareholders, the shareholder representative appointed by the institution performing the duties of a contributor shall exercise the rights in accordance with Article 13 of this Law.
When the board of directors of the company makes a resolution on a transaction between the company and an affiliate, the director involved in the transaction shall not exercise the voting right, nor shall they exercise the voting right on behalf of other directors.

When a wholly state-owned enterprise, wholly state-owned company, or state-controlled company undergoes merger, division, restructuring, transfer of major assets, making external investments with non-monetary assets, liquidation, or other circumstances where asset appraisal shall be conducted according to laws, administrative regulations, and the enterprise's articles of association, the relevant assets shall be appraised in accordance with regulations.

A wholly state-owned enterprise, wholly state-owned company, or state-controlled company shall entrust a qualified asset appraisal institution established according to law to conduct asset appraisal; if matters that shall be reported to the institution performing the duties of a contributor for decision are involved, the situation of entrusting the asset appraisal institution shall be reported to the institution performing the duties of a contributor.

A wholly state-owned enterprise, wholly state-owned company, or state-controlled company and its directors, supervisors, and senior officers shall truthfully provide relevant information and materials to the asset appraisal institution, and shall not collude with the asset appraisal institution in appraising and pricing.

Article 50 An asset appraisal institution and its staff members, when entrusted to appraise relevant assets, shall comply with laws, administrative regulations and the appraisal practice standards, and shall appraise the entrusted assets independently, objectively and impartially. The asset appraisal institution shall be responsible for the appraisal report it issues.

Article 51 For the purposes of this Law, the transfer of State-owned assets means the act of transferring, according to law, the rights and interests formed by the State's capital contribution to an enterprise to other entities or individuals, except where the State-owned assets are transferred gratuitously in accordance with the State regulations.

Article 52 The transfer of State-owned assets shall facilitate the strategic adjustment of the layout and structure of the State-owned economy, prevent the loss of State-owned assets, and shall not impair the legitimate rights and interests of the parties to the transaction.

Article 53 The transfer of State-owned assets shall be decided by the institution performing the duties of a contributor. Where the institution performing the duties of a contributor decides to transfer all of the State-owned assets, or to transfer part of the State-owned assets such that the State no longer has a controlling stake in the enterprise, it shall report to the people's government at the same level for approval.

Article 54 The transfer of State-owned assets shall follow the principles of value-for-money and compensated transfer, openness, fairness and impartiality.
Except where the transfer may be conducted directly through negotiation in accordance with the State regulations, the transfer of State-owned assets shall be conducted openly on the property rights trading venues established according to law. The transferor shall truthfully disclose the relevant information and solicit transferees; where there are two or more transferees resulting from the solicitation, the transfer shall be conducted by way of public bidding.
The transfer of listed shares shall be governed by the provisions of the Securities Law of the People's Republic of China.

Article 55 The transfer of State-owned assets shall take as the basis the price which has been appraised according to law, recognized by the institution performing the duties of a contributor, or approved by the people's government at the same level upon the report of the institution performing the duties of a contributor, and the minimum transfer price shall be reasonably determined.

Article 56 Where the laws, administrative regulations or the State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Institution of the State Council provide that State-owned assets may be transferred to the directors, supervisors, senior officers of the enterprise or their close relatives, or to enterprises owned or actually controlled by such persons, when such assets are transferred, if the aforesaid persons or enterprises participate in the transfer as a transferee, they shall bid equally with other transferee participants; the transferor shall truthfully disclose the relevant information in accordance with the relevant State regulations; the relevant directors, supervisors and senior officers shall not participate in the formulation and organization of the implementation of any work related to the transfer plan.
Article 57 The transfer of State-owned assets to overseas investors shall comply with the relevant State regulations and shall not endanger national security and public interests.

Article 58 The State shall establish and improve the budget system for state capital operations, and shall implement budget management over the income obtained from state capital and the expenditures thereof.

Article 60 The state capital operating budget shall be prepared separately on an annual basis, incorporated into the budget of the people's government at the corresponding level, and submitted to the people's congress at the corresponding level for approval.
Expenditures in the state capital operating budget shall be arranged in accordance with the size of the budget revenue for the current year, and no deficit shall be recorded.

Article 61 The finance departments of the State Council and the relevant local people's governments shall be responsible for the compilation of the draft state capital operating budget, and the institution performing the functions of a contributor shall submit to the finance department a proposed draft of the state capital operating budget for which it performs the functions of a contributor.

Article 62 The specific measures and implementation steps for the administration of the state capital operating budget shall be prescribed by the State Council and filed with the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress.

Article 63 The standing committees of the people's congresses at all levels shall, according to law, exercise their supervisory powers by hearing and deliberating special work reports on the performance of the functions of a contributor by the people's government at the corresponding level and on the supervision and administration of state-owned assets, and by organizing law enforcement inspections on the implementation of this Law.
Article 64 The State Council and local people's governments shall supervise the performance of duties by the institutions authorized by them to perform the functions of a contributor.

Article 65 The audit institutions of the State Council and local people's governments shall, in accordance with the provisions of the Audit Law of the People's Republic of China, conduct audit supervision over the implementation of the state capital operating budget and over state-invested enterprises that are subject to audit supervision.

Article 66 The State Council and local people's governments shall, according to law, disclose to the public the status of state-owned assets and the work of supervision and administration of state-owned assets, and shall accept supervision by the public.
Any entity or individual shall have the right to report and accuse any act that causes losses to state-owned assets.

Article 67 The institution performing the functions of a contributor may, as needed, entrust an accounting firm to audit the annual financial and accounting reports of a wholly state-owned enterprise or a wholly state-owned company, or through a resolution of the shareholders' meeting or the general meeting of shareholders of a state-controlled company, have the state-controlled company engage an accounting firm to audit the annual financial and accounting reports of the company, so as to safeguard the rights and interests of the contributor.

Article 69 Where a staff member of the institution performing the duties of a capital contributor is derelict of duty, abuses his or her power, or engages in malpractices for personal gain, if the act does not constitute a crime, disciplinary action shall be taken according to law.

Article 70 Where a shareholder representative appointed by the institution performing the duties of a capital contributor fails to perform his or her duties in accordance with the instructions of the appointing institution, thereby causing losses to state-owned assets, he or she shall bear compensation liability according to law; if he or she is a state functionary, disciplinary action shall also be taken according to law.

Article 72 Where, in transaction activities involving related-party transactions, transfer of state-owned assets, etc., the parties maliciously collude to impair the rights and interests of state-owned assets, such transaction shall be void.

Article 73 Where a director, supervisor, or senior officer of a wholly state-owned enterprise, wholly state-owned company, or state-controlled company violates the provisions of this Law, causing significant losses to state-owned assets, and is removed from office, he or she shall not serve as a director, supervisor, or senior officer of a wholly state-owned enterprise, wholly state-owned company, or state-controlled company within five years from the date of removal; if he or she causes particularly significant losses to state-owned assets, or is sentenced to criminal punishment for embezzlement, bribery, misappropriation of property, or sabotage of the socialist market economic order, he or she shall be permanently disqualified from serving as a director, supervisor, or senior officer of a wholly state-owned enterprise, wholly state-owned company, or state-controlled company.

Article 74 Where an asset appraisal institution or an accounting firm that is entrusted to conduct asset appraisal or financial audit of a state-invested enterprise violates the provisions of laws, administrative regulations, and professional standards, and issues a false asset appraisal report or audit report, legal liability shall be imposed in accordance with the provisions of relevant laws and administrative regulations.
Article 75 Whoever violates the provisions of this Law, if the act constitutes a crime, shall be investigated for criminal liability according to law.
Article 76 Where laws or administrative regulations provide otherwise for the management and supervision of state-owned assets of financial enterprises, such provisions shall apply.
Article 77 This Law shall come into force as of May 1, 2009.
